title: {{cast.mark}}'s agent runs a tool on the {{vocab.agentcore}}, as {{cast.mark}}
goal: {{cast.mark}}'s agent needs to run a tool on the {{vocab.agentcore}} on {{cast.mark}}'s behalf, under its own workload identity, without a shared service credential and without handing the runtime {{cast.mark}}'s own token.
obstacle: The runtime accepts only tokens its own issuer minted, and an ID-JAG is a grant for an authorization server to redeem, never an access token. A shared service account would hide who acted.
control: Lab simulation, no AWS service called: the exchange issuer turns the caller token into an ID-JAG (leg 1, RFC 8693), the runtime's issuer redeems it (leg 2, RFC 7523) and mints the runtime's access token with {{cast.mark}} as sub and the agent in act, and the runtime runs the tool under the workload identity that token resolves to.
say: The AWS side is mocked. The point is the shape: the ID-JAG stops at an authorization server, and the runtime sees a workload identity plus who it acted for.

steps.title: The agent hands {{cast.mark}}'s caller token to the runner
steps.tell: The exchange issuer signed {{cast.mark}} in and issued a caller token. The runner starts from it and never sees the session.
steps.say: The agent's credential is a token with one audience, not a shared secret.

steps.title: Leg 1: exchange it for an ID-JAG
steps.tell: The runner exchanges the caller token at the exchange issuer (RFC 8693). The result is an ID-JAG addressed to the runtime's issuer, with {{cast.mark}} as sub and the calling client in act.
steps.say: The assertion names {{cast.mark}} and says who is acting for them.
steps.why: Delegation is in the token, not in a shared account.

blocked.tell: Point Exchange.Resource somewhere else. The ID-JAG is addressed to the wrong issuer, and leg 2 refuses it.
blocked.say: An assertion is redeemable by the issuer it names, and by no one else.

steps.title: Leg 2: redeem it at the runtime's issuer
steps.tell: The runner posts the ID-JAG to the runtime's issuer (RFC 7523). The issuer checks signature, audience, expiry, client and a single-use jti, and mints its own access token with {{cast.mark}} as sub, the agent in act, and the workload identity resolved.
steps.say: The runtime's own issuer decides, and it mints its own token.
steps.why: Without a redemption the ID-JAG is worthless to a runtime.

steps.title: The runtime runs the tool under the workload identity
steps.tell: The runner invokes the mock AgentCore runtime with the redeemed access token. The runtime verifies it against its own issuer's keys, sees {{cast.mark}} as sub and the agent in act, and answers the tool under the workload identity.
steps.say: The runtime logs the workload identity, not a shared service account.
steps.why: The agent has its own identity, and the human is still in the token.

steps.title: What the runtime refuses
steps.tell: {{cast.mark}}'s original caller token is refused: a different issuer minted it. The raw ID-JAG is refused too: it is a grant for an issuer to redeem, never an access token for a runtime.
steps.say: The refusal names the check that failed, from the runtime's own answer.
steps.why: An ID-JAG stops at an authorization server; only its redeemed token moves on.

proof.happy: The runtime answers the tool call, naming {{cast.mark}} as sub, the agent in act, and the workload identity.
proof.blocked: The runtime refuses {{cast.mark}}'s original token (signature) and the raw ID-JAG (token type), each naming the check that failed.
